problems: The TFAP2C and EHF occupancy qualifications in F1 and F3 should be updated: E25 and E26 report peaks containing the variant. These are not allele-specific results, and the biosamples do not establish occupancy in a cleft-relevant cell type (EHF's nearest summit is 262 bp away).
IRF6 has gene–disease support in E27, but the element-to-IRF6 link remains indirect: the L2G and eQTL evidence is not a perturbation of this element, and the eQTL tissues are not cleft-relevant.

The cleft association reports A as the effect allele (E07), whereas F1, F3, and F5 predict greater binding to G. No cleft-cell gene-expression or functional evidence establishes whether these binding directions increase or decrease cleft risk; the ref-favored predictions in F2 and F4 likewise do not establish a causal direction.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping TFAP2C ChIP peak would provide in-vivo occupancy evidence and help distinguish F1 from the other proposed TF chains.
A variant-overlapping EHF ChIP peak would provide in-vivo occupancy evidence for the F3 candidate.
This can clarify the strength and evidence type of the IRF6–cleft association, though it will not by itself prove regulation by this element.

critique.next_experiment: In a cleft-relevant craniofacial cell model, compare A and G alleles for TFAP2C, EHF, ZNF143, TEAD1, and ELF1 occupancy (for example, allele-specific CUT&RUN or ChIP). Then perturb EH38E2863563 in the same model and measure IRF6 expression to test the unresolved element-to-gene link.

lookups.why: A variant-overlapping TFAP2C ChIP peak would provide in-vivo occupancy evidence and help distinguish F1 from the other proposed TF chains.
A variant-overlapping EHF ChIP peak would provide in-vivo occupancy evidence for the F3 candidate.
This can clarify the strength and evidence type of the IRF6–cleft association, though it will not by itself prove regulation by this element.

games.reason: Both chains have comparable in-vitro allele-binding predictions and share the same element, gene, cell-type, and phenotype evidence. TFAP2C is better supported because ReMap reports two TFAP2C ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant, whereas the ZNF143 evidence is only a summit 33 bp away in K-562. Neither has expression evidence in the supplied context, and the binding predictions alone do not establish in-vivo allele-specific occupancy.

Both chains have only in-vitro predictions for their allele-specific binding, and neither has expression evidence in a matched cleft-relevant context. But TFAP2C has ReMap peaks containing the variant in two biosamples, with a summit 27 bp away (E25), whereas ZNF143’s reported summit is 33 bp elsewhere in K-562, not at the variant (E14). The predicted alt-favored TFAP2C binding is also consistent with its chain’s stated direction (E13).
